Cookie Policy

Last updated: November 27, 2026

What cookies are

Cookies are small text files that a website can store on your device. Websites use them to remember settings, keep you signed in, or measure and track visits.

Our use of cookies

This website uses analytics cookies only if you accept them. When you first visit, a banner asks whether we may use Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity. Until you press Accept, neither tool loads and no analytics cookies are set. If you press Decline, they stay off.

We use no advertising cookies, and we turn off Google's advertising features: ad storage and ad personalization stay off even if you accept.

Analytics we use if you accept

  • Google Analytics 4 gives us usage statistics: which pages are visited, how visitors arrive, how far they scroll, which links and buttons they click, and their device type and approximate location. It sets the cookies _ga and _ga_*, which last up to two years.
  • Microsoft Clarity shows us how pages are used through heatmaps and session recordings of clicks, scrolling and mouse movement. What you type into forms is masked, so it is not recorded. It sets the cookies _clck, which lasts up to a year, and _clsk, which lasts a day.

Google and Microsoft process this data under their own privacy policies. We use it only to understand how the website is used and to improve it. See our Privacy Policy.

Remembering your choice

Your browser's local storage keeps your answer to the banner (accept or decline) so we do not ask again on every page. This is not a cookie, it does not identify you, and it stays on your device.

Changing your choice

Use the Cookie choices button at the bottom of any page to open the banner again, then press Accept or Decline. If you decline after accepting, measurement stops from that point. Cookies already set stay in your browser until they expire or you delete them in your browser settings.

Other third-party requests

Some features make requests to other services, and those services may process technical data such as your IP address and browser details:

  • Google Fonts supplies the website's fonts when a page loads.
  • Web3Forms receives what you typed when you submit the demo form, and emails it to us.

These requests are explained in our Privacy Policy. Their providers have their own policies.

Controlling cookies in your browser

You can also block or delete cookies in your browser settings, and most browsers let you block third-party requests with extensions. Each browser does this differently, so check its help pages. Blocking cookies will not stop this website from working.

Changes to this policy

If we change the cookies or tools we use, we will update this policy first. The date at the top of this page shows when it last changed.
